# Performance Management

`customer_support.support_management.performance_management` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**Is this agent meeting the standard, measured against the work they were actually given?**


> Judging whether an agent is meeting the standard, with consequences attached. It is the only capability in this subdomain where the answer goes on a record, and that fact governs how every input to it must be treated: any measure used here will be optimised, so the measure has to be one that is harmless when gamed. Throughput and handle time fail that test immediately — both improve when an agent closes tickets that were not finished. The defensible version compares an agent against the queue they actually worked rather than against the team, because queue mix explains more variance in every support metric than individual skill does.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **experimental**


> Promote by adding outcomes, failure_modes, playbooks, heuristics, mental_models, decision_frameworks, kpis and handoffs, following quality-assurance in this subdomain. The hardest thing to get right, and the thing worth writing down first, is the relationship with quality_assurance: QA scores exist to teach, and the moment they are admissible as evidence here, honest self-reporting stops and the sample stops describing the work. Some organisations accept that trade deliberately; the file should say which trade is being made rather than leave it implicit. Second is the volume-versus-quality trap — every metric that rewards closing tickets rewards closing them prematurely, and reopen rate is the only cheap correction.
